newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan puts jubilee building up for sale.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan puts jubilee building up for sale.

text.p: Pakistan's government said on Saturday it wanted to sell Islamabad's Convention Centre, built by the previous administration to become a national monument.

A statement by the government's Privatisation Commission invited "expression of interest" from prospective bidders for the centre, which cost 646 million rupees ($16 million) when it was built to host a conference in March to mark Pakistan's golden jubiliee.

The government of prime minister Benazir Bhutto ordered the construction of centre as a monument to the 50th anniversary of Pakistan's creation from the partition and independence of British India in 1947.
But she was sacked last November on disputed charges of misrule before she could preside over March's summit meeting of the 54-nation Organisation of Islamic Conference.

Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government, which took office in February after his Pakistan Muslim League party won a landslide election victory, has described the building as wasteful for a cash-strapped nation.

"The government is planning for either the divestiture of its share in the Convention Centre and the transfer of 100 percent ownership to the private sector or (giving it) on a long-term lease basis," the statement said.
A successful bidder will be allowed to develop the land for commercial purposes, such as a hotel, shopping mall or recreational facilities, it said.
